properties.name: A686 Penrith–Alston
properties.reason: Scenic high-level A-road with sustained bends, gradients and exposed sections; suitable for a Transporter-sized campervan with normal mountain-road care.

properties.name: B6277 Alston–Middleton-in-Teesdale
properties.reason: Remote moorland B-road with bends, gradients and winter exposure; generally manageable but slower than trunk-road alternatives.

properties.name: A689 Stanhope–Alston
properties.reason: High moorland route with steep and exposed sections; suitable in good conditions but merits care in poor weather.

properties.name: A169 Pickering–Whitby
properties.reason: Main cross-moors A-road and a sensible campervan route despite gradients and bends.

properties.name: Rosedale Chimney Bank
properties.reason: Exceptionally steep, narrow hill road with severe gradients and tight geometry. Avoid by default in a campervan when practical alternatives exist.

properties.name: A171 Whitby–Scarborough
properties.reason: Principal coastal A-road and the sensible through-route for campervans between Whitby and Scarborough.

properties.name: B1257 Helmsley–Stokesley
properties.reason: Long rural B-road with bends, villages and moorland sections; normally suitable for a Transporter-sized campervan with care.

properties.name: A684 Leyburn–Hawes
properties.reason: Main Wensleydale through-route and generally straightforward for campervans, with normal village and tourist traffic caveats.

properties.name: Fleet Moss road Hawes–Oughtershaw
properties.reason: Narrow, steep and exposed high-level road with limited passing; usable by a compact campervan but best treated as a deliberate scenic drive rather than a shortcut.

properties.name: A623 Chapel-en-le-Frith–Baslow
properties.reason: Established cross-Peak A-road and a sensible through-route for campervans.

properties.name: A515 Ashbourne–Buxton
properties.reason: Major north-south Peak District corridor and generally straightforward for campervans.

properties.name: Winnats Pass
properties.reason: Very steep, narrow-sided pass with tight bends and tourist traffic. A compact campervan can fit, but it is a deliberate route rather than the easiest approach to Castleton.

properties.name: A537 Cat and Fiddle
properties.reason: Wide enough for normal traffic but highly sinuous and exposed; suitable for campervans with appropriate speed and weather awareness.

properties.name: A494 Dolgellau–Bala
properties.reason: Principal regional A-road and a sensible campervan route between Dolgellau and Bala.

properties.name: A487 Machynlleth–Dolgellau
properties.reason: Main coastal/trunk corridor and generally the preferred route for campervans over minor alternatives.

properties.name: A4069 Black Mountain Road
properties.reason: Mountain A-road with sweeping bends, gradients and exposed sections; generally suitable for a Transporter-sized campervan but weather and visibility matter.

properties.name: A470 Brecon–Merthyr Tydfil
properties.reason: Strategic north-south trunk route and a straightforward campervan corridor.

properties.name: A39 Porlock–Lynmouth
properties.reason: Main Exmoor coastal route but steep and bendy in places, including Porlock Hill; suitable for a compact campervan with appropriate gear and speed management.

properties.name: Porlock Toll Road
properties.reason: Private scenic alternative to Porlock Hill with gradients and bends but historically used as a gentler route; check current opening and toll conditions before relying on it.

properties.name: A396 Dunster–Tiverton
properties.reason: Useful cross-Exmoor route with narrow, bendy and wooded sections; manageable for a compact campervan but slower than its A-road status may suggest.
